events.title: The First Airline Flight
events.body: The St Petersburg–Tampa Airboat Line carries its first paying passenger across Tampa Bay — 23 minutes, one passenger, and the birth of scheduled air travel.

events.title: The Tramp First Appears
events.body: Charlie Chaplin's Little Tramp shuffles onto screen in Kid Auto Races at Venice — bowler, cane and all. Within two years he is the most famous face on Earth.

events.title: The Rokeby Venus Slashed
events.body: Suffragette Mary Richardson attacks Velázquez's masterpiece in the National Gallery with a meat cleaver, protesting Emmeline Pankhurst's imprisonment.

events.title: The King at the Cup Final
events.body: George V becomes the first reigning monarch to attend an FA Cup final, watching Burnley beat Liverpool 1–0 at Crystal Palace.

events.title: Franz Ferdinand Assassinated
events.body: Gavrilo Princip shoots the Austro-Hungarian heir and his wife Sophie in Sarajevo. The driver had taken a wrong turn. Within six weeks, Europe is at war.

events.title: The National Party Founded
events.body: General JBM Hertzog founds the National Party in Bloemfontein — the party that will rule South Africa from 1948 and build apartheid.

events.title: Gandhi Leaves South Africa
events.body: After 21 years, Mohandas Gandhi sails from Cape Town for the last time. The methods of satyagraha, forged against South African race laws, go with him to India.

events.title: Austria-Hungary Declares War
events.body: One month after Sarajevo, Vienna declares war on Serbia and shells Belgrade. The alliances begin to pull every great power in.

events.title: The London Stock Exchange Closes
events.body: Panic selling forces the Exchange to shut for the first time in its history. It stays closed for five months; New York follows the same day.

events.title: Germany Declares War on Russia
events.body: The Tsar's mobilisation triggers Germany's declaration. France mobilises the same day. The continental war is now unstoppable.

events.title: Britain Declares War on Germany
events.body: Germany invades neutral Belgium; Britain's ultimatum expires at 23:00. "The lamps are going out all over Europe," says Foreign Secretary Edward Grey.

events.title: The First Electric Traffic Light
events.body: Cleveland, Ohio installs the world's first electric traffic signal at Euclid Avenue and East 105th Street — red and green, with a warning buzzer.

events.title: Endurance Sets Sail
events.body: Ernest Shackleton's Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition leaves Plymouth — toward one of the greatest survival stories ever lived.

events.title: The Panama Canal Opens
events.body: The SS Ancon makes the first official transit, joining the Atlantic and Pacific. Ten years of American engineering — and thousands of workers' lives — behind it.

events.title: The Battle of Mons
events.body: The British Expeditionary Force fights its first battle of the war, its riflemen firing so fast the Germans believe they face machine guns.

events.title: The Library of Louvain Burns
events.body: German troops torch the Belgian university library — 300,000 books and irreplaceable mediaeval manuscripts lost in a night that shocks the world.

events.title: The Last Passenger Pigeon Dies
events.body: Martha, the last of a species that once darkened American skies in the billions, dies in Cincinnati Zoo — extinction's most famous single moment.

events.title: Benedict XV Elected Pope
events.body: Giacomo della Chiesa becomes pope as Europe burns. He calls the war "the suicide of civilised Europe" and spends his papacy pleading for peace.

events.title: The Battle of the Marne
events.body: French and British forces stop the German sweep towards Paris; Parisian taxis ferry troops to the front. The war of movement ends — the trenches begin.

events.title: Home Rule — Passed and Frozen
events.body: Irish Home Rule finally receives royal assent after decades of struggle, then is immediately suspended for the war — a postponement with fateful consequences.

events.title: The Maritz Rebellion
events.body: Martial law is declared in South Africa as Boer officers rise against joining Britain's war on Germany. The revolt is crushed by year's end.

events.title: First Ypres Begins
events.body: The armies dig in around the Flemish town where so much of the war's horror will concentrate. By its end, the old British regular army has effectively ceased to exist.

events.title: The Christmas Truce
events.body: Along stretches of the Western Front, the guns fall silent. Soldiers sing carols, swap tobacco, bury their dead — and, in places, play football between the trenches.

events.title: Biafra Surrenders
events.body: The Nigerian Civil War ends after 30 months and perhaps two million deaths, most from starvation — the famine that taught television audiences the word Biafra.

events.title: The 747 Enters Service
events.body: Pan Am flies the first Boeing 747 from New York to London. The jumbo jet makes long-haul flying a mass-market affair.

events.title: The Chicago Seven Verdict
events.body: Five of the seven anti-war activists are convicted of crossing state lines to incite riot — all convictions later overturned, the trial itself the real spectacle.

events.title: Rhodesia Declares a Republic
events.body: Ian Smith's government cuts its last tie to the Crown, entrenching white-minority rule — and deepening the bush war that follows.

events.title: The Non-Proliferation Treaty
events.body: The NPT enters into force, dividing the world into five nuclear powers and everyone else — still the backbone of arms control.

events.title: McCartney Announces the Split
events.body: A Q&A in his solo album's press kit confirms it: the Beatles are over. The most influential band in pop history dissolves into lawsuits.

events.title: "Houston, We've Had a Problem"
events.body: An oxygen tank explodes aboard Apollo 13, 330,000 km from Earth. Four days of improvised engineering bring the crew home alive — NASA's finest failure.

events.title: The First Earth Day
events.body: Twenty million Americans march for the environment — the largest single-day protest yet held, and the start of the modern environmental movement.

events.title: Kent State Shootings
events.body: National Guardsmen fire on anti-war students in Ohio, killing four. The photograph of a girl screaming over a body becomes the image of a divided America.

events.title: The Kent State Photograph
events.body: Student photographer John Filo captures 14-year-old Mary Ann Vecchio kneeling over the body of Jeffrey Miller, arms raised. It wins the Pulitzer Prize and becomes the image of America turning its guns on its own young.

events.title: “Ohio”
events.body: Neil Young writes it after seeing the Kent State photographs; Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young record it within weeks and rush it out as a single. “Four dead in Ohio” — the angriest protest song of its era, banned by some American radio stations.

events.title: Heath Wins the Election
events.body: Edward Heath's Conservatives defeat Harold Wilson against the polls' predictions — the government that will take Britain into Europe.

events.title: Pelé's Third World Cup
events.body: Brazil's 4–1 demolition of Italy in Mexico City crowns perhaps the greatest team ever fielded. Pelé becomes the only player to win three World Cups.

events.title: The Aswan High Dam Completed
events.body: Egypt tames the Nile's flood after eleven years of work, creating Lake Nasser — and submerging ancient Nubia, whose temples were moved stone by stone.

events.title: Jimi Hendrix Dies
events.body: The guitarist who rewired the electric guitar dies in London at 27 — the age that will claim Joplin weeks later and Morrison within a year.

events.title: Nasser Dies
events.body: Egypt's president, the voice of Arab nationalism, dies of a heart attack at 52. Five million mourners fill Cairo's streets.

events.title: De Gaulle Dies
events.body: The general who twice saved France dies at home playing patience. "France is a widow," says President Pompidou.

events.title: The Bhola Cyclone
events.body: The deadliest tropical cyclone ever recorded kills perhaps half a million people in East Pakistan — and the botched relief effort feeds the push for Bangladeshi independence.

events.title: Venera 7 Lands on Venus
events.body: The Soviet probe makes the first fully successful landing on another planet, transmitting from a surface hot enough to melt lead.

events.title: Idi Amin Seizes Uganda
events.body: The army commander takes power in a coup while President Obote is abroad. Eight years of terror follow, with hundreds of thousands killed.

events.title: Decimal Day
events.body: Britain retires shillings and old pence after centuries: 100 new pence to the pound. The nation grumbles, adapts, and moves on within weeks.

events.title: The Fight of the Century
events.body: Joe Frazier hands Muhammad Ali his first professional defeat at Madison Square Garden — two unbeaten heavyweight champions, and an event that stops the world.

events.title: Bangladesh Declares Independence
events.body: East Pakistan proclaims itself Bangladesh as the Pakistani army launches a brutal crackdown. A nine-month liberation war begins.

events.title: Salyut 1 — the First Space Station
events.body: The Soviet Union launches the first station into orbit, opening the era of living in space.

events.title: Jim Morrison Dies
events.body: The Doors' frontman is found dead in a Paris bathtub at 27, joining what will be called the 27 Club.

events.title: Internment in Northern Ireland
events.body: British forces arrest hundreds without trial in dawn raids. The policy backfires spectacularly, driving recruitment to the IRA.

events.title: The Nixon Shock
events.body: The United States ends the dollar's convertibility to gold, demolishing the Bretton Woods system — modern floating currencies date from this Sunday broadcast.

events.title: Greenpeace Sets Sail
events.body: A chartered fishing boat leaves Vancouver to protest a nuclear test in Alaska. The voyage fails; the organisation it births does not.

events.title: Walt Disney World Opens
events.body: The Florida resort opens on 11,000 hectares of drained swamp — soon the most visited holiday destination on Earth.

events.title: China Takes Its UN Seat
events.body: The General Assembly votes to seat the People's Republic and expel Taiwan — Beijing joins the Security Council's permanent five.

events.title: The First Microprocessor
events.body: Intel advertises the 4004 — a complete computer processor on one chip. Everything digital that follows descends from this sliver of silicon.

events.title: Shoot
events.body: In a small gallery in Santa Ana, Chris Burden has a friend shoot him in the arm with a .22 rifle in front of a few witnesses. With Vietnam's violence nightly on American television, the performance asks what it means to watch someone be shot.

events.title: Bangladesh Wins Its War
events.body: Pakistani forces surrender in Dhaka to India and the Mukti Bahini. Bangladesh is free; the war's atrocities leave wounds that never fully close.

events.title: A Clockwork Orange Opens
events.body: Kubrick's ultraviolent satire scandalises Britain; after copycat-crime claims, he withdraws it from UK screens himself for 27 years.

events.title: Bloody Sunday
events.body: British paratroopers shoot 26 unarmed civil-rights marchers in Derry, killing 14. The Troubles' deadliest year follows.

events.title: Nixon Goes to China
events.body: The arch anti-communist lands in Beijing to meet Mao — a week that redraws the Cold War map and gives diplomacy a new proverb.

events.title: The Limits to Growth
events.body: A team at MIT runs a computer model of population, industry and resources and warns that growth cannot go on forever on a finite planet. Launched in Washington, it sells millions and frames the environmental argument for decades.

events.title: The Godfather Opens
events.body: Coppola's Corleone saga redefines the American film — and makes an offer audiences can't refuse.

events.title: Ceylon Becomes Sri Lanka
events.body: The island declares itself a republic, shedding its colonial name and the British Crown.

events.title: SALT I Signed
events.body: Nixon and Brezhnev sign the first treaty limiting nuclear arsenals — détente's high-water mark.

events.title: The Stockholm Conference
events.body: The first UN conference on the environment opens — the moment environmental protection becomes international politics.

events.title: The Terror of War
events.body: Associated Press photographer Nick Ut photographs nine-year-old Phan Thi Kim Phuc running naked down a road after a napalm strike near Trang Bang. The image wins the Pulitzer and helps turn world opinion against the war.

events.title: Ziggy Stardust Arrives
events.body: David Bowie releases The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust — pop's greatest reinvention artist invents the rock alter ego.

events.title: The Watergate Break-In
events.body: Five men are arrested bugging Democratic headquarters in Washington. A "third-rate burglary" begins the unravelling of a presidency.

events.title: The Man Died
events.body: Wole Soyinka's prison notes from two years in detention during the Nigerian civil war, much of it in solitary confinement, written in secret between the lines of books and on scraps. “The man dies in all who keep silent in the face of tyranny.”

events.title: Fischer Beats Spassky
events.body: The American genius takes the world chess title from the Soviet Union in Reykjavik — a Cold War fought in 64 squares.

events.title: The Munich Massacre
events.body: Palestinian gunmen seize Israeli athletes at the Olympics; eleven die in a botched rescue. Terror arrives at the Games.

events.title: M*A*S*H Comes to Television
events.body: The Korean War dramedy begins its eleven-year run — a Vietnam-era protest wearing a 1950s uniform.

events.title: Miracle in the Andes
events.body: A plane carrying a Uruguayan rugby team crashes in the mountains. Sixteen survive 72 days — a story of endurance that still staggers.

events.title: Pong Launches
events.body: Atari's bat-and-ball game lands in a California bar and promptly breaks from overuse. The video game industry begins with two paddles and a square ball.

events.title: The Blue Marble
events.body: Apollo 17 — the last Moon mission — photographs the whole Earth, lit and alone. It becomes one of the most reproduced images in history.

events.title: Britain Joins Europe
events.body: The UK enters the European Economic Community after two French vetoes — the start of a 47-year membership.

events.title: Roe v Wade
events.body: The US Supreme Court rules abortion a constitutional right — the most contested American judgment of the century.

events.title: The Paris Peace Accords
events.body: America signs its way out of Vietnam after a decade of war and 58,000 US dead. The war itself has two years left.

events.title: The Dark Side of the Moon
events.body: Pink Floyd releases an album about madness, money and time — it stays on the charts for over 900 weeks.

events.title: CITES Signed
events.body: Eighty nations agree to control trade in endangered species — ivory, rhino horn, rare orchids and all.

events.title: The First Mobile Phone Call
events.body: Motorola's Martin Cooper stands on a New York pavement and phones his rival at Bell Labs — from a handheld portable telephone. The mobile age begins with a gloat.

events.title: The World Trade Center Opens
events.body: The twin towers are dedicated in Manhattan — briefly the tallest buildings on Earth.

events.title: Skylab Launches
events.body: America's first space station reaches orbit damaged, is repaired by its crew in orbit — and proves people can live and work in space for months.

events.title: Secretariat's Belmont
events.body: The chestnut colt wins the Triple Crown by 31 lengths in world-record time — widely called the greatest racehorse performance ever.

events.title: Small Is Beautiful
events.body: E. F. Schumacher's essays on “economics as if people mattered” appear in the year of the oil shock, arguing for human-scale technology and an end to treating natural resources as income.

events.title: Bruce Lee Dies
events.body: The martial artist who carried kung fu to the world dies in Hong Kong at 32, a month before Enter the Dragon makes him a global icon.

events.title: The Chilean Coup
events.body: Pinochet's forces bomb the presidential palace; Salvador Allende dies inside. Seventeen years of dictatorship begin.

events.title: The Yom Kippur War
events.body: Egypt and Syria attack Israel on its holiest day. Three weeks of war redraw Middle East politics — and reach into every petrol tank on Earth.

events.title: The Oil Embargo
events.body: Arab producers cut supply and ban sales to Israel's allies. Oil prices quadruple; queues form at petrol pumps across the West. The post-war boom ends here.

events.title: The Sydney Opera House Opens
events.body: Jørn Utzon's white sails open after 14 scandal-plagued years — the architect, forced out, never returns to see it. It becomes the symbol of a continent.

events.title: The Gulag Archipelago
events.body: Smuggled out on microfilm and first published in Paris, Solzhenitsyn's history of the Soviet labour camps, built from his own imprisonment and hundreds of survivors' testimonies. Within weeks Moscow expels him.

events.title: The Exorcist Opens
events.body: Audiences faint in the aisles at William Friedkin's possession tale — the horror film becomes a cultural event.

events.title: Solzhenitsyn Expelled
events.body: The USSR deports the author of The Gulag Archipelago, the book that demolished Soviet moral standing abroad. He spends 20 years in exile.

events.title: The Terracotta Army Found
events.body: Farmers digging a well in Shaanxi strike the buried army of China's first emperor — 8,000 clay soldiers, no two faces alike.

events.title: The Carnation Revolution
events.body: Portugal's army overthrows Europe's oldest dictatorship almost without a shot, carnations in their rifle barrels — and Portugal's African empire begins to dissolve.

events.title: I Like America and America Likes Me
events.body: Joseph Beuys flies to New York, is carried by ambulance wrapped in felt to a SoHo gallery, and spends three days locked in a room with a wild coyote — a meditation on an America split by Vietnam and by its treatment of Native peoples.

events.title: India Tests the Bomb
events.body: The "Smiling Buddha" test makes India the sixth nuclear power — the first outside the Security Council's five.

events.title: The Arpilleras of Chile
events.body: From the mid-1970s, women whose husbands and sons have been disappeared stitch scraps of cloth into small tapestries showing raids, prisons and empty chairs. Smuggled abroad and sold, the arpilleras carry testimony the junta cannot censor.

events.title: All the President's Men
events.body: Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein's account of how two young Washington Post reporters followed a burglary to the Oval Office. Published weeks before Nixon resigns; filmed two years later.

events.title: West Germany Win the World Cup
events.body: Beckenbauer's hosts beat Cruyff's total-footballing Netherlands 2–1 in Munich — the brilliant losers remembered better than the winners.

events.title: Nixon Resigns
events.body: Facing impeachment over Watergate, Richard Nixon becomes the first US president to resign. "Our long national nightmare is over," says Gerald Ford.

events.title: Haile Selassie Deposed
events.body: Ethiopia's emperor — 44 years on the throne, Rastafari's living god — is driven from his palace in a Volkswagen. The Derg's red terror follows.

events.title: The Rumble in the Jungle
events.body: Ali rope-a-dopes the fearsome George Foreman in Kinshasa and reclaims the title at 32 — the most mythologised fight in boxing.

events.title: The Arecibo Message
events.body: Astronomers beam humanity's first deliberate radio greeting at a star cluster 25,000 light years away — a postcard that will outlive its senders.

events.title: The Birmingham Pub Bombings
events.body: IRA bombs kill 21 people in two city-centre pubs. Six innocent men are convicted and serve 16 years — one of Britain's worst miscarriages of justice.

events.title: Lucy Is Found
events.body: In Ethiopia's Afar desert, scientists unearth a 3.2-million-year-old skeleton that walked upright — and name her after the Beatles song playing in camp.

events.title: Cyclone Tracy
events.body: A compact, ferocious cyclone destroys most of Darwin on Christmas morning; the city is evacuated and rebuilt from scratch.

events.title: Microsoft Founded
events.body: Two school friends, Bill Gates and Paul Allen, start a company in Albuquerque to sell BASIC for a hobbyist computer.

events.title: The Khmer Rouge Take Phnom Penh
events.body: Pol Pot's forces empty Cambodia's capital at gunpoint within days. Year Zero begins; a quarter of the nation will die.

events.title: The Fall of Saigon
events.body: Helicopters lift the last Americans from embassy rooftops as North Vietnamese tanks crash the palace gates. The Vietnam War ends.

events.title: Jaws Opens
events.body: Spielberg's shark empties beaches and fills cinemas — the first summer blockbuster, and the template for forty years of them.

events.title: Mozambique Independent
events.body: Frelimo takes power after a decade of armed struggle as Portugal withdraws — a new front-line state on South Africa's border.

events.title: North
events.body: Seamus Heaney's collection sets the violence of the Troubles beside Iron Age bodies preserved in the bogs — asking what a poet owes to his tribe, and to the truth, when his country is at war with itself.

events.title: Arthur Ashe Wins Wimbledon
events.body: The first black men's champion outsmarts the unstoppable Jimmy Connors — Ashe, once refused a visa by apartheid South Africa, wins with his head.

events.title: Handshake in Orbit
events.body: An Apollo and a Soyuz dock 220 km up; Stafford and Leonov shake hands through the hatch — détente's most photogenic moment.

events.title: The Helsinki Accords
events.body: Thirty-five nations freeze Europe's borders and — almost as an afterthought — sign up to human rights. Dissidents behind the Iron Curtain take note.

events.title: Bohemian Rhapsody Released
events.body: Queen's six-minute mock-operatic single — too long, said the label — tops the UK chart for nine weeks and becomes the national earworm.

events.title: Angola Independent
events.body: Portugal departs and the MPLA declares independence in Luanda — as South African and Cuban forces pour into a civil war that will burn for 27 years.

events.title: The Whitlam Dismissal
events.body: Australia's Governor-General sacks the elected Prime Minister — the gravest constitutional crisis in the country's history. "Well may we say God save the Queen..."

events.title: Franco Dies
events.body: Spain's dictator of 36 years dies in his bed. King Juan Carlos, his chosen successor, chooses democracy instead.

events.title: Concorde Enters Service
events.body: Simultaneous take-offs from London and Paris open supersonic passenger flight — Mach 2, champagne, and London to New York in three and a half hours.

events.title: The Argentine Coup
events.body: A military junta seizes Argentina; in the Dirty War that follows, up to 30,000 people are disappeared.

events.title: Apple Founded
events.body: Jobs, Wozniak and the soon-departed Ronald Wayne start a computer company in a California garage.

events.title: The Ramones' Debut
events.body: Fourteen songs in under half an hour. Punk rock's starting pistol, fired from Queens, New York.

events.title: The Soweto Uprising
events.body: Police open fire on schoolchildren marching against Afrikaans instruction; hundreds die in the months that follow. The photograph of dying Hector Pieterson wakes the world.

events.title: The Photograph of Hector Pieterson
events.body: Sam Nzima of The World photographs Mbuyisa Makhubo carrying the dying 13-year-old Hector Pieterson, his sister Antoinette running beside them. Published worldwide, it makes Soweto impossible to ignore — and forces Nzima out of photography.

events.title: The American Bicentennial
events.body: Two hundred years after the Declaration, tall ships fill New York Harbour and fireworks blanket the nation.

events.title: The Raid on Entebbe
events.body: Israeli commandos fly 4,000 km to Uganda and free 102 hijacked hostages in a 90-minute raid — the operation's only fallen soldier is Yoni Netanyahu.

events.title: The Perfect 10
events.body: Fourteen-year-old Nadia Comăneci scores gymnastics' first Olympic 10.0 in Montreal — the scoreboard, unable to show it, reads 1.00.

events.title: Viking 1 Lands on Mars
events.body: The first successful Mars lander sends back photographs of a rust-red, rock-strewn plain — and tests the soil for life.

events.title: The Tangshan Earthquake
events.body: A magnitude-7.6 quake levels a sleeping industrial city in China, killing at least 240,000 — the deadliest earthquake of the century.

events.title: Mao Dies
events.body: The Chairman dies at 82 having remade and ravaged China — within weeks his widow and her Gang of Four are arrested, and the Deng era beckons.

events.title: Carter Elected
events.body: A peanut farmer and one-term Georgia governor defeats Gerald Ford — the post-Watergate outsider's victory.

events.title: Rocky Opens
events.body: Stallone, broke, refuses to sell his script unless he stars. The underdog film about an underdog wins Best Picture.

events.title: Anarchy in the UK
events.body: The Sex Pistols release punk's manifesto single; within weeks a sweary TV interview makes them national villains — and household names.

events.title: The Pompidou Opens
events.body: Piano and Rogers turn the building inside out, pipes and escalators on the facade. Paris is horrified, then proud.

events.title: The Tenerife Disaster
events.body: Two 747s collide on a fog-bound runway; 583 die — aviation's deadliest accident, and the reason cockpit culture was rebuilt around plain speaking.

events.title: Star Wars Opens
events.body: A space fantasy no studio wanted becomes the biggest film ever made and rewires popular culture. "A long time ago, in a galaxy far, far away..."

events.title: The Apple II Goes on Sale
events.body: The first mass-market personal computer that ordinary people could love — colour graphics, a keyboard, and a decade-long production run.

events.title: Dispatches
events.body: Michael Herr's fevered reportage from Vietnam — written over a decade, in the language of the grunts — is often called the best book about the war. He went on to co-write Apocalypse Now and Full Metal Jacket.

events.title: The New York Blackout
events.body: Lightning knocks out the city for 25 hours; looting and arson scar a thousand stores — and block parties with liberated turntables feed the rise of hip-hop.

events.title: Elvis Dies
events.body: The King is found dead at Graceland at 42. Eighty thousand people line the streets of Memphis; the myth only grows.

events.title: Voyager 1 Launches
events.body: Carrying a golden record of Earth's sounds, the probe sets out on the Grand Tour — bound, eventually, for interstellar space.

events.title: Steve Biko Dies in Detention
events.body: The Black Consciousness leader dies of brain injuries after police interrogation in Pretoria. "His death leaves me cold," says the justice minister. The world does not forget.

events.title: The Last Case of Smallpox
events.body: Somali cook Ali Maow Maalin develops the last natural case in history — the final link in a chain stretching back millennia.

events.title: Sadat Flies to Jerusalem
events.body: Egypt's president does the unthinkable — lands in Israel and addresses the Knesset. "No more war," he says. Peace, and his own death warrant, follow.

events.title: Saturday Night Fever Opens
events.body: Travolta's strut and the Bee Gees' falsetto send disco global — the soundtrack becomes one of the best-selling albums ever.

events.title: Chaplin Dies
events.body: The Little Tramp dies on Christmas morning in Switzerland at 88 — the first face the whole world knew.

events.title: The First GPS Satellite
events.body: The US Air Force launches Navstar 1 — the first block of a system that will one day guide every phone, ship and delivery van on Earth.

events.title: The Amoco Cadiz
events.body: The supertanker breaks apart off Brittany, spilling 220,000 tonnes of crude along 300 km of coast — then the largest oil spill in history.

events.title: The Saur Revolution
events.body: Communist officers seize Kabul in a bloody coup — the first domino in forty years of Afghan war.

events.title: Aldo Moro Found Dead
events.body: Italy's former prime minister, kidnapped 55 days earlier by the Red Brigades, is found in a car boot in Rome — the darkest hour of the Years of Lead.

events.title: Grease Opens
events.body: Travolta and Newton-John's 1950s pastiche becomes the highest-grossing musical film yet — and a sleepover staple for generations.

events.title: Argentina Win at Home
events.body: Ticker-tape, Kempes, and a 3–1 final win over the Dutch — a World Cup of genuine brilliance staged by a murderous junta.

events.title: I Write What I Like
events.body: A collection of Steve Biko's writings, many first published under the pen-name Frank Talk, appears in London the year after his death. Banned in South Africa, it becomes a founding text of Black Consciousness.

events.title: The Power of the Powerless
events.body: Václav Havel's samizdat essay imagines a greengrocer who stops putting a slogan in his shop window — and in doing so begins to “live within the truth”. Copied by hand across the Eastern bloc, it inspires the movements that topple communism.

events.title: The Emperor
events.body: Ryszard Kapuściński interviews the servants, courtiers and pillow-bearers of Haile Selassie's palace to portray the decay of a court and the fall of an absolute ruler.

events.title: The First IVF Baby
events.body: Louise Brown is born in Oldham, conceived in a Petri dish. Twelve million IVF births follow in the next half-century.

events.title: Black Friday in Tehran
events.body: Troops fire on protesters in Jaleh Square, killing dozens. Compromise with the Shah dies with them; revolution becomes inevitable.

events.title: Ali Makes History
events.body: Muhammad Ali outpoints Leon Spinks in New Orleans to win the heavyweight title an unprecedented third time.

events.title: The Camp David Accords
events.body: Thirteen days at a presidential retreat produce the framework for peace between Egypt and Israel — Begin and Sadat share the Nobel; Sadat pays with his life.

events.title: A Polish Pope
events.body: Karol Wojtyła becomes John Paul II — the first non-Italian pope in 455 years, and a quiet earthquake behind the Iron Curtain.

events.title: Jonestown
events.body: Over 900 followers of Jim Jones die in a mass murder-suicide in the Guyanese jungle — the cult tragedy that gives the language a terrible phrase.

events.title: Khomeini Returns to Iran
events.body: Two weeks after the Shah flees, the Ayatollah lands in Tehran before millions. Within months Iran is an Islamic Republic.

events.title: The Dinner Party
events.body: Judy Chicago's triangular banquet table, with 39 place settings for women of history and 999 more names on the porcelain floor, opens in San Francisco. A landmark of feminist art, built to answer women's erasure from the record.

events.title: Three Mile Island
events.body: A reactor partially melts down in Pennsylvania. Casualties: none confirmed. Confidence in nuclear power: shattered for a generation.

events.title: Thatcher Takes Office
events.body: Britain's first woman prime minister enters Downing Street quoting St Francis of Assisi. Eleven and a half years of upheaval begin.

events.title: Alien Opens
events.body: "In space no one can hear you scream." Ridley Scott fuses horror and science fiction — and Ripley rewrites the action hero.

events.title: The Walkman Goes on Sale
events.body: Sony's cassette player makes music portable and personal — the soundtrack moves inside your head.

events.title: “Zimbabwe”
events.body: Bob Marley's anthem on the album Survival — “Every man got a right to decide his own destiny” — is sung by guerrilla fighters in the bush war. Months later Marley plays it at Zimbabwe's independence celebrations.

events.title: Burger's Daughter
events.body: Nadine Gordimer's novel of a white communist's daughter, set around the Soweto uprising, is banned in South Africa within weeks — then unbanned after protests. Gordimer later wins the Nobel Prize.

events.title: Skylab Falls
events.body: America's space station re-enters over the Indian Ocean and Western Australia, scattering debris; an Australian shire fines NASA $400 for littering.

events.title: The Sandinistas Take Managua
events.body: Somoza flees and the guerrillas enter the capital, ending a 43-year family dictatorship — and lighting the fuse of the Contra war.

events.title: Apocalypse Now
events.body: Francis Ford Coppola's hallucinatory Vietnam epic, shot in the Philippines through typhoons and a heart attack, opens in America. Four years after Saigon fell, cinema starts to reckon with the war.

events.title: Mountbatten and Warrenpoint
events.body: The IRA kills Lord Mountbatten with a boat bomb and 18 soldiers in an ambush at Warrenpoint — the Troubles' bloodiest day for the British establishment.

events.title: Rapper's Delight
events.body: The Sugarhill Gang put fifteen minutes of party rhymes on vinyl — hip-hop leaves the block party and enters the charts.

events.title: The Hostage Crisis Begins
events.body: Iranian students storm the US embassy in Tehran and take 52 Americans hostage — for 444 days that poison US–Iran relations to this day.

events.title: The Wall Released
events.body: Pink Floyd's double album of alienation gives the world an anthem of schoolroom rebellion — and, a decade on, a soundtrack for actual walls falling.

events.title: Lancaster House
events.body: After three months of talks in London, Rhodesia's war ends with an agreement for elections — the path to Zimbabwe.

events.title: The Soviets Invade Afghanistan
events.body: Airborne troops seize Kabul on Christmas Eve; a nine-year quagmire begins that helps bring down the USSR itself.

events.title: Bon Scott Dies
events.body: AC/DC's frontman is found dead in a car in East Dulwich, London, at 33. The band nearly folds — then records Back in Black in his honour five months later.

events.title: Miracle on Ice
events.body: A squad of American college players beats the mighty Soviet Union 4–3 at the Lake Placid Winter Olympics. It is still ranked among the greatest upsets in sport.

events.title: St Pauls Riot, Bristol
events.body: A police raid on the Black and White Café sparks hours of rioting in Bristol's St Pauls district — an early warning of the urban unrest that will mark the decade in Britain.

events.title: Terry Fox Begins the Marathon of Hope
events.body: Having lost a leg to cancer, the 21-year-old Canadian dips his artificial limb in the Atlantic and sets out to run across Canada for cancer research — a marathon a day.

events.title: Zimbabwe Becomes Independent
events.body: Rhodesia becomes Zimbabwe at midnight, with Robert Mugabe as Prime Minister. Bob Marley plays the independence celebrations in Harare.

events.title: Operation Eagle Claw Fails
events.body: The US mission to rescue the Tehran embassy hostages collapses in the desert; eight servicemen die when a helicopter and transport plane collide.

events.title: SAS Storms the Iranian Embassy
events.body: After a six-day siege in London, the SAS abseils down the building and ends the standoff in 17 minutes — live on television. One hostage is killed; five gunmen die.

events.title: Smallpox Declared Eradicated
events.body: The World Health Assembly formally declares smallpox eradicated — the first human disease ever wiped out, after a 13-year global vaccination campaign.

events.title: Mount St Helens Erupts
events.body: The Washington State volcano explodes with the force of hundreds of atomic bombs, flattening 600 square kilometres of forest and killing 57 people.

events.title: The Empire Strikes Back Opens
events.body: The darker Star Wars sequel lands — and "No, I am your father" becomes one of cinema's most misquoted lines.

events.title: Pac-Man Debuts in Japan
events.body: Namco releases Puck Man in Tokyo arcades. Renamed for export, Pac-Man becomes the highest-grossing arcade game of all time.

events.title: CNN Launches
events.body: Ted Turner's Cable News Network goes on air in Atlanta — the world's first 24-hour television news channel.

events.title: MK Sabotages Sasol
events.body: Umkhonto we Sizwe guerrillas bomb the Sasol synthetic-fuel plants, sending fireballs over Secunda and Sasolburg — the ANC's most spectacular strike inside South Africa to date.

events.title: Waiting for the Barbarians
events.body: J. M. Coetzee's allegory of a frontier magistrate who discovers the torture carried out in his empire's name — written in South Africa in the years after Steve Biko died in police custody.

events.title: Borg's Fifth Straight Wimbledon
events.body: Björn Borg outlasts John McEnroe in a final crowned by an 18–16 fourth-set tiebreak — often called the greatest tennis match ever played.

events.title: Moscow Olympics Open Amid Boycott
events.body: The Games open with more than 60 nations staying away over the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan. Britain attends; its athletes march under the Olympic flag.

events.title: Back in Black Released
events.body: AC/DC's tribute to Bon Scott, fronted by new singer Brian Johnson, goes on to sell over 50 million copies — one of the best-selling albums in history.

events.title: Bologna Station Bombing
events.body: A bomb in the Bologna railway station waiting room kills 85 people — Italy's deadliest post-war terrorist attack, attributed to neo-fascists.

events.title: “Biko”
events.body: Peter Gabriel's lament for Steve Biko, framed by South African funeral song and ending with the line “the eyes of the world are watching now”. Banned in South Africa, it becomes a human-rights anthem.

events.title: Solidarity Is Born
events.body: Striking shipyard workers in Gdańsk, led by electrician Lech Wałęsa, win the right to form the Soviet bloc's first independent trade union.

events.title: Iran–Iraq War Begins
events.body: Iraq invades Iran, expecting a quick victory. The war grinds on for eight years, kills perhaps a million people, and draws in the world's navies.

events.title: "The Lady's Not for Turning"
events.body: With unemployment soaring, Margaret Thatcher tells the Conservative conference she will not reverse course — the defining phrase of her premiership.

events.title: Reagan Wins the Presidency
events.body: Ronald Reagan defeats Jimmy Carter in a landslide, carrying 44 states and ushering in the conservative era that will define the decade.

events.title: Voyager 1 Reaches Saturn
events.body: The probe skims past Saturn, returning the first close images of its rings and moons before being flung out of the plane of the planets forever.

events.title: John Lennon Shot in New York
events.body: The former Beatle is murdered outside the Dakota building by a man he had signed an autograph for hours earlier. Millions mourn worldwide.

events.title: Greece Joins the EEC
events.body: Greece becomes the tenth member of the European Economic Community — the bloc's first expansion into the Mediterranean.

events.title: Reagan Inaugurated; Hostages Freed
events.body: Minutes after Reagan is sworn in, Iran releases the 52 American hostages it has held for 444 days — a pointed parting snub to Jimmy Carter.

events.title: The First London Marathon
events.body: Some 6,700 runners set off from Greenwich in the rain. The race becomes one of the world's great marathons — and a fancy-dress institution.

events.title: Reagan Shot
events.body: John Hinckley Jr shoots the President outside a Washington hotel. Reagan, 70, survives surgery and jokes with his doctors: "I hope you're all Republicans."

events.title: Brixton Riots
events.body: Three days of rioting in south London leave hundreds injured and lead to the Scarman Report on policing and race — a landmark in British social history.

events.title: First Space Shuttle Flight
events.body: Columbia thunders off the pad at Cape Canaveral — the first reusable spacecraft, launched 20 years to the day after Gagarin's flight.

events.title: Mitterrand Elected
events.body: François Mitterrand becomes the Fifth Republic's first Socialist president, ending 23 years of right-wing rule in France.

events.title: Cats Opens in the West End
events.body: Andrew Lloyd Webber sets T. S. Eliot's poems to music at the New London Theatre. Critics are baffled; audiences queue for 21 years.

events.title: Pope John Paul II Shot
events.body: Mehmet Ali Ağca shoots the Pope in St Peter's Square. He survives four hours of surgery — and later visits his would-be assassin in prison to forgive him.

events.title: First Report of AIDS
events.body: The CDC describes a rare pneumonia in five young men in Los Angeles — the first official report of what will be named AIDS a year later.

events.title: Israel Bombs the Osirak Reactor
events.body: Israeli jets destroy Iraq's nearly-complete nuclear reactor outside Baghdad in a surprise raid condemned by the UN Security Council.

events.title: Raiders of the Lost Ark Opens
events.body: Spielberg and Lucas introduce Indiana Jones — whip, hat and all. It is the year's biggest film and spawns one of cinema's great franchises.

events.title: Terry Fox Dies
events.body: Cancer claims the Marathon of Hope runner at 22, after 5,373 km of his run. Annual Terry Fox Runs have since raised hundreds of millions for research.

events.title: Woza Albert!
events.body: Percy Mtwa, Mbongeni Ngema and Barney Simon devise a two-man play imagining Christ's second coming in apartheid South Africa. Born at Johannesburg's Market Theatre, it tours the world with nothing but two actors and a few crates.

events.title: Prisoner Without a Name, Cell Without a Number
events.body: Newspaper editor Jacobo Timerman's account of his arrest, torture and imprisonment by Argentina's junta — one of the first books to show the world the inside of the Dirty War.

events.title: Toxteth Riots
events.body: Rioting erupts in Liverpool's Toxteth district; CS gas is used on the British mainland for the first time. The unrest spreads to other English cities.

events.title: ¡Ay Sudamérica!
events.body: The Chilean art collective CADA hires light aircraft to scatter thousands of leaflets over a working-class district of Santiago, declaring that each person who works for the expansion of life is an artist — poetry as an act of defiance under Pinochet.

events.title: Botham's Ashes Miracle
events.body: Following on at Headingley, England are 500-1 with the bookies — then Ian Botham's unbeaten 149 and Bob Willis's 8 for 43 steal an 18-run win over Australia.

events.title: Charles Marries Diana
events.body: An estimated 750 million people watch the wedding at St Paul's Cathedral — the "fairytale wedding" that will not end as one.

events.title: MTV Launches
events.body: "Ladies and gentlemen, rock and roll." The first video played is Video Killed the Radio Star — and music television changes pop forever.

events.title: IBM PC Launches
events.body: The IBM 5150 arrives with an open architecture and Microsoft's DOS — the template for decades of personal computing.

events.title: Only Fools and Horses Debuts
events.body: Del Boy and Rodney Trotter first appear on BBC One. The sitcom becomes one of Britain's best-loved programmes.

events.title: Guernica Comes Home
events.body: Picasso's 1937 cry against the bombing of Guernica arrives in Madrid. He had refused to let it enter Spain until democracy returned; six years after Franco's death, it finally does.

events.title: The TGV Enters Service
events.body: France's high-speed train begins running Paris to Lyon at 260 km/h — the fastest scheduled trains in the world, and the model for high-speed rail everywhere.

events.title: Sadat Assassinated
events.body: Egypt's president, who made peace with Israel, is gunned down by Islamist soldiers during a victory parade in Cairo. Hosni Mubarak succeeds him.

events.title: Martial Law in Poland
events.body: General Jaruzelski declares martial law overnight, interning Solidarity's leaders. Tanks on the streets of Warsaw; the union goes underground.

events.title: Venera 13 Lands on Venus
events.body: The Soviet probe survives 127 minutes at 457°C — and sends back the first colour photographs taken on the surface of another planet.

events.title: Argentina Invades the Falklands
events.body: Argentine forces seize the islands; Britain assembles a naval task force within days. A ten-week war in the South Atlantic begins.

events.title: Canada Patriates Its Constitution
events.body: The Queen signs the Constitution Act in Ottawa, giving Canada full control of its own constitution and a new Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

events.title: ZX Spectrum Launches
events.body: Clive Sinclair's £125 home computer, with its rubber keys and rainbow flash, puts programming into a generation of British bedrooms.

events.title: The Belgrano Is Sunk
events.body: HMS Conqueror torpedoes the Argentine cruiser General Belgrano; 323 men die — the war's single greatest loss of life.

events.title: HMS Sheffield Hit
events.body: An Exocet missile strikes the destroyer HMS Sheffield, killing 20 — the first Royal Navy ship lost in action since the Second World War.

events.title: Spain Joins NATO
events.body: Spain becomes the alliance's 16th member — its first expansion since 1955, six years after Franco's death.

events.title: Israel Invades Lebanon
events.body: Israeli forces push into Lebanon to drive out the PLO, beginning a siege of Beirut and an occupation whose consequences last decades.

events.title: E.T. Opens
events.body: Spielberg's story of a boy and a stranded alien becomes the highest-grossing film yet made, holding the record for over a decade.

events.title: Argentine Surrender at Stanley
events.body: The Falklands War ends after 74 days. The toll: 255 British, 649 Argentine and 3 islander lives. Thatcher's political fortunes are transformed.

events.title: Prince William Born
events.body: The first child of Charles and Diana arrives at St Mary's Hospital, Paddington — second in line to the throne.

events.title: Blade Runner Opens
events.body: Ridley Scott's rain-soaked vision of 2019 Los Angeles flops at the box office — then grows into one of the most influential science-fiction films ever made.

events.title: The House of the Spirits
events.body: Isabel Allende, niece of the murdered president, began it as a letter to her dying grandfather in exile. Three generations of a family carry the novel to a military coup that is unmistakably Chile's.

events.title: Destination Biafra
events.body: Buchi Emecheta's novel of the Nigerian civil war, told through a young woman who crosses the lines — one of the first novels to set the war at the centre of women's experience.

events.title: Shah of Shahs
events.body: Kapuściński, holed up in a Tehran hotel after the revolution, pieces together the reign and fall of Mohammad Reza Pahlavi from photographs, notes and conversations.

events.title: Intruder in the Queen's Bedroom
events.body: Michael Fagan scales a drainpipe at Buckingham Palace and sits on the Queen's bed while she talks to him — one of the great royal security scandals.

events.title: Italy Win the World Cup
events.body: Paolo Rossi's goals power Italy past West Germany 3–1 in Madrid. President Pertini's celebrations in the stands become as famous as the final.

events.title: Hyde Park and Regent's Park Bombings
events.body: IRA bombs kill 11 military bandsmen and cavalrymen in London's royal parks, along with seven horses, during changing-of-the-guard ceremonies.

events.title: “Shipbuilding”
events.body: Written by Elvis Costello and Clive Langer during the Falklands War and sung by Robert Wyatt: a quiet song about dying shipyard towns that will profit from building warships for the sons they'll send to die.

events.title: Princess Grace Dies
events.body: Grace Kelly, Hollywood star turned Princess of Monaco, dies at 52 after her car plunges off a mountain road above Monte Carlo.

events.title: Sabra and Shatila Massacre
events.body: Lebanese Christian militiamen massacre hundreds of Palestinian refugees in Beirut camps controlled by the Israeli army — an atrocity that shocks the world.

events.title: Kohl Becomes Chancellor
events.body: Helmut Kohl takes office in West Germany after a no-confidence vote — beginning a 16-year chancellorship that will span reunification.

events.title: The First CD Player Goes on Sale
events.body: Sony's CDP-101 launches in Japan alongside the first compact discs. Digital sound begins its takeover of the living room.

events.title: The Mary Rose Rises
events.body: Henry VIII's flagship is lifted from the Solent seabed after 437 years, watched live on television by millions.

events.title: García Márquez Wins the Nobel
events.body: The Colombian author of One Hundred Years of Solitude takes the Nobel Prize in Literature — magical realism's coronation on the world stage.

events.title: The Vietnam Veterans Memorial
events.body: A black granite wall cut into the earth in Washington, carrying the names of over 58,000 dead, is dedicated. Its designer, Maya Lin, was a 21-year-old student; her design was bitterly attacked, then became the most visited memorial in the capital.

events.title: Thriller Released
events.body: Michael Jackson's sixth album, with Billie Jean and Beat It, becomes the best-selling album of all time — a title it still holds.

events.title: First Permanent Artificial Heart
events.body: Retired dentist Barney Clark receives the Jarvik-7 artificial heart in Utah and lives 112 days — a milestone in medical engineering.

events.title: The Internet's Birthday
events.body: ARPANET switches to TCP/IP, the common language that lets separate networks connect to each other. Many mark this as the day the internet began.

events.title: Seat Belts Become Law in the UK
events.body: Front-seat passengers must now buckle up. Compliance jumps from 40% to 90% within weeks, and road deaths fall sharply.

events.title: M*A*S*H Says Goodbye
events.body: The Korean War comedy's finale draws roughly 106 million American viewers — the most-watched scripted broadcast in television history.

events.title: “Sunday Bloody Sunday”
events.body: U2 open their album War with a drumbeat like gunfire and a refusal: “I won't heed the battle call.” Written about the Derry killings of 1972; on stage Bono would introduce it: “This is not a rebel song.”

events.title: The Swatch Launches
events.body: Switzerland's answer to the quartz crisis: a cheap, colourful, collectable plastic watch. It saves the Swiss watch industry by refusing to take itself seriously.

events.title: Hawke Elected in Australia
events.body: Former union leader Bob Hawke sweeps Labor to power — beginning the longest Labor government in Australian history.

events.title: Reagan Announces "Star Wars"
events.body: The President unveils the Strategic Defense Initiative — a plan to shoot down missiles from space that critics dub Star Wars and Moscow takes deadly seriously.

events.title: The £1 Coin Arrives
events.body: Britain's round pound enters circulation, replacing the £1 note in England and Wales. The note is withdrawn five years later.

events.title: The Moonwalk, Broadcast
events.body: On the Motown 25 TV special, Michael Jackson glides backwards through Billie Jean — and the moonwalk becomes the decade's signature dance move.

events.title: Church Street Bombing, Pretoria
events.body: An MK car bomb outside air force headquarters kills 19 people and wounds more than 200 — the deadliest attack of the armed struggle inside South Africa.

events.title: The AIDS Virus Identified
events.body: Luc Montagnier's team in Paris publishes the isolation of the virus later named HIV — the discovery that wins the 2008 Nobel Prize.

events.title: Return of the Jedi Opens
events.body: The original Star Wars trilogy concludes with Ewoks, a second Death Star and the redemption of Darth Vader.

events.title: Thatcher's Landslide
events.body: Boosted by the Falklands and a divided opposition, the Conservatives win a 144-seat majority — the largest since 1945.

events.title: Sally Ride Makes History
events.body: Aboard Challenger, the 32-year-old physicist becomes the first American woman in space — 20 years after the Soviets' Valentina Tereshkova.

events.title: The citizen
events.body: Richard Hamilton paints a Republican prisoner on the blanket protest in the Maze prison, from television footage — a diptych of a long-haired figure and his excrement-smeared cell walls, as unsettling as it is sympathetic.

events.title: A Few South Africans
events.body: Sue Williamson begins a series of portraits of women in the struggle, Winnie Mandela among them, printed small and cheaply so they could circulate at a time when many of these women were banned and could not be quoted.

events.title: Nintendo's Famicom Launches
events.body: The Family Computer goes on sale in Japan. Exported as the NES, it will revive a crashed games industry and bring Mario to the world.

events.title: KAL 007 Shot Down
events.body: A Soviet fighter destroys a Korean airliner that strayed into Soviet airspace, killing all 269 aboard and plunging the Cold War to a new low.

events.title: The First Commercial Mobile Phone
events.body: US regulators approve Motorola's DynaTAC 8000X — a 790-gram "brick" costing $3,995, and the start of the mobile age.

events.title: The Siluetazo
events.body: On the Day of Spring, as the junta's grip weakens, artists and the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo trace thousands of life-size human silhouettes in the Plaza de Mayo — one for each of the disappeared — and paste them on the walls of Buenos Aires.

events.title: The Man Who Saved the World
events.body: Soviet officer Stanislav Petrov judges a missile-attack warning to be a false alarm and declines to report it as real — possibly averting nuclear war.

events.title: Australia II Takes the America's Cup
events.body: The winged-keel yacht ends the New York Yacht Club's 132-year hold on the trophy — the longest winning streak in sport.

events.title: Wałęsa Wins the Nobel Peace Prize
events.body: The interned Solidarity leader is honoured for non-violent struggle; fearing exile, he sends his wife Danuta to Oslo to collect it.

events.title: Beirut Barracks Bombings
events.body: Suicide truck bombs kill 241 US and 58 French peacekeepers in their barracks — the deadliest day for the US Marines since Iwo Jima.

events.title: US Invades Grenada
events.body: American forces seize the Caribbean island after a Marxist coup — the first major US combat operation since Vietnam, criticised by Britain whose Queen is Grenada's head of state.

events.title: South Africa's Tricameral Referendum
events.body: White voters approve a new constitution giving coloured and Indian South Africans separate chambers — and black South Africans nothing. Resistance organises in response.

events.title: Harrods Bombing
events.body: An IRA car bomb outside the Knightsbridge store kills six people in the Christmas shopping crowds.

events.title: AT&T Breakup Takes Effect
events.body: The court-ordered breakup of AT&T splits the US telecoms giant into seven regional 'Baby Bells' — the largest corporate breakup in US history. It paves the way for deregulation and eventually the conditions in which the modern internet industry develops.

events.title: "Where's the Beef?"
events.body: Wendy's launches the advert that eats American culture — three old ladies, one tiny patty. Walter Mondale borrows the line in a presidential debate within weeks.

events.title: Apple Macintosh Launched
events.body: Apple introduces the Macintosh during a Super Bowl advertisement directed by Ridley Scott. Priced at $2,495, the Mac features a graphical user interface and mouse — making these concepts accessible to consumers for the first time. It changes the trajectory of personal computing.

events.title: First Untethered Spacewalk
events.body: NASA astronaut Bruce McCandless II becomes the first human to float freely in space without any physical connection to a spacecraft. The resulting photograph — a lone figure against the black of space — becomes one of the most iconic images of the space age.

events.title: Torvill and Dean Win Olympic Gold
events.body: British ice dancers Torvill and Dean win Olympic gold at Sarajevo with a perfect score — all nine judges award maximum 6.0 for their Boléro routine. Watched by approximately 24 million people in the UK alone, it remains one of the most watched sports moments in British television history.

events.title: UK Miners' Strike Begins
events.body: The National Union of Mineworkers begins a national strike against proposed pit closures — the most bitter industrial confrontation in post-war British history. It lasts nearly a year, leaving lasting consequences for British industry, communities, and the labour movement.

events.title: “Free Nelson Mandela”
events.body: Jerry Dammers of The Special AKA writes a joyous ska protest tune about a man most British listeners had never heard of. It reaches the UK top ten and turns Mandela's name into a chant around the world.

events.title: Starlight Express Opens
events.body: Lloyd Webber's trains-on-roller-skates spectacle opens at the Apollo Victoria, with the entire theatre rebuilt as a racetrack.

events.title: HIV Identified as Cause of AIDS
events.body: US Health Secretary Margaret Heckler announces that researcher Robert Gallo has identified HIV as the cause of AIDS. The announcement ends intense scientific uncertainty and opens the path toward diagnostic tests and eventually antiretroviral treatment.

events.title: China Opens 14 Coastal Cities
events.body: China opens 14 coastal cities to foreign direct investment as part of Deng Xiaoping's accelerating economic reform programme, dramatically expanding the Special Economic Zone model pioneered in Shenzhen.

events.title: Operation Blue Star — Golden Temple
events.body: The Indian Army storms the Golden Temple in Amritsar — the holiest site in Sikhism — killing militant leader Bhindranwale and hundreds of others. It directly leads to the assassination of Indira Gandhi five months later.

events.title: Tetris Created
events.body: Soviet software engineer Alexey Pajitnov creates Tetris at the Soviet Academy of Sciences in Moscow. The falling-block puzzle game spreads through floppy disk copies before reaching Western markets — becoming one of the best-selling games in history.

events.title: Ghostbusters Released
events.body: Ivan Reitman's Ghostbusters opens starring Bill Murray, Dan Aykroyd, Harold Ramis, and Sigourney Weaver. One of the highest-grossing films of 1984, it defines a template for blockbuster entertainment that studios follow for decades.

events.title: The Tin-Pot Foreign General and the Old Iron Woman
events.body: Raymond Briggs, creator of The Snowman, publishes a savage picture-book satire of the Falklands War — two leaders squabbling over a wet island while ordinary young men die.

events.title: Los Angeles Olympics Open
events.body: The XXIII Summer Olympics open in Los Angeles, producing memorable moments including Carl Lewis winning four gold medals. Despite the Soviet-led boycott, the Games turn a profit and reshape how cities approach Olympic hosting.

events.title: Born in the USA Released
events.body: Bruce Springsteen releases Born in the USA — one of the best-selling albums of the decade. The title track is widely misread as patriotic rather than the Vietnam veteran critique it actually is, including by Ronald Reagan's campaign.

events.title: Nunca Más
events.body: Novelist Ernesto Sabato's commission hands President Alfonsín its report on the disappeared: almost 9,000 documented cases and hundreds of secret detention centres. “Never again” becomes a bestseller and evidence at the trial of the juntas.

events.title: IRA Brighton Hotel Bombing
events.body: The Provisional IRA detonates a bomb at Brighton's Grand Hotel during the Conservative Party conference, targeting Prime Minister Thatcher and her cabinet. Five are killed, 31 injured. Thatcher escapes unhurt.

events.title: Jerzy Popiełuszko Murdered
events.body: Father Jerzy Popiełuszko, a Polish Catholic priest and Solidarity supporter, is abducted and murdered by Polish secret police. His death galvanises opposition to Communist rule. His funeral is attended by an estimated 350,000 people.

events.title: The Famine Report
events.body: Michael Buerk's BBC report from Korem, filmed by Mohamed Amin, describes a “biblical famine” in Ethiopia. Bob Geldof sees it that evening; within a month he has recorded Band Aid.

events.title: Indira Gandhi Assassinated
events.body: Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi is shot dead by two Sikh bodyguards in New Delhi, following Operation Blue Star. Her son Rajiv Gandhi is sworn in hours later. Anti-Sikh riots kill thousands in the following days.

events.title: The Killing Fields
events.body: Roland Joffé's film tells the story of the reporter Dith Pran's survival of Pol Pot's Cambodia. Haing S. Ngor, himself a survivor of the camps, wins an Oscar for playing him.

events.title: Do They Know It's Christmas? Recorded
events.body: Bob Geldof and Midge Ure assemble Band Aid to record a charity single for Ethiopian famine relief in a single day. It becomes the fastest-selling UK single in chart history at the time.

events.title: Bhopal Gas Disaster
events.body: A catastrophic gas leak at the Union Carbide plant in Bhopal, India kills thousands overnight — the world's worst industrial disaster. Questions of corporate accountability remain unresolved decades later.

events.title: The Bhopal Photograph
events.body: Pablo Bartholomew photographs the burial of an unidentified child, eyes still open, in the soil of Bhopal. The image wins World Press Photo of the Year and becomes the face of the disaster.

events.title: Sino-British Declaration on Hong Kong
events.body: The UK agrees to transfer Hong Kong to China on 1 July 1997 under 'one country, two systems.' The declaration sets in motion a countdown that defines Hong Kong's political identity for generations.

events.title: Reagan's Second Inauguration
events.body: Ronald Reagan is inaugurated for his second term. The ceremony is moved indoors due to -14°C temperatures. His landslide over Walter Mondale gave him 49 of 50 states — one of the largest electoral margins in US history.

events.title: First Mobile Networks Launch in UK
events.body: Vodafone and Cellnet launch the UK's first mobile phone networks. The first call on Vodafone is made by comedian Ernie Wise. Handsets are the size of house bricks. Almost nobody believes mobile phones will become mass market.

events.title: IRA Mortar Attack — Newry
events.body: The Provisional IRA kills nine RUC officers in Newry — the single largest loss of life for the RUC in the Troubles. The attack accelerates back-channel talks between the British and Irish governments.

events.title: UK Miners' Strike Ends
events.body: The British miners' strike collapses after nearly a year without a deal. Thatcher's victory fundamentally reshapes British trade unionism and accelerates deindustrialisation.

events.title: Gorbachev Becomes Soviet Leader
events.body: Mikhail Gorbachev becomes General Secretary of the Communist Party at 54. His policies of glasnost and perestroika will reshape the Cold War and ultimately dissolve the USSR.

events.title: Air Jordan 1 Released
events.body: Nike releases Michael Jordan's banned black-and-red sneaker to the public. Sportswear becomes street fashion, and the sneaker economy is born.

events.title: Ozone Hole Confirmed
events.body: Scientists at the British Antarctic Survey confirm dramatic thinning of the ozone layer. The discovery leads directly to the Montreal Protocol of 1987 — the most successful international environmental agreement in history.

events.title: New Coke Launched
events.body: Coca-Cola replaces its 99-year-old formula, triggering one of history's most spectacular marketing failures. By July, the original formula is reinstated as 'Coca-Cola Classic.'

events.title: Bradford City Stadium Fire
events.body: 56 people die when fire engulfs the main stand at Bradford City's stadium. The wooden stand is destroyed in under four minutes. The disaster leads to sweeping changes in UK stadium safety legislation.

events.title: Dennis Taylor Wins World Snooker
events.body: Dennis Taylor defeats Steve Davis 18–17 on the final black ball just before midnight, watched by an estimated 18.5 million in the UK — still a record for post-midnight television. The match transforms snooker into a mainstream cultural event.

events.title: Heysel Stadium Disaster
events.body: 39 people die when a wall collapses at Heysel Stadium in Brussels before the European Cup Final between Liverpool and Juventus. English clubs are banned from European football for five years.

events.title: Commodore Amiga Launched
events.body: Commodore launches the Amiga 1000 in New York. With its multitasking OS, colour graphics, and stereo sound, it is years ahead of rivals — the machine of choice for creative computing and a cult favourite.

events.title: TWA Flight 847 Hijacked
events.body: TWA Flight 847 is hijacked by Hezbollah militants in a 17-day crisis. US Navy diver Robert Stethem is murdered. The hijacking sharpens global debate about negotiating with terrorists.

events.title: Afghan Girl
events.body: Steve McCurry's portrait of a green-eyed girl in a refugee camp near Peshawar appears on the cover of National Geographic — one of the most recognised photographs ever printed, and a face for the millions displaced by the Soviet war.

events.title: South Africa Declares State of Emergency
events.body: The South African government declares a state of emergency in 36 districts following escalating anti-apartheid unrest. Over the following months, more than 7,500 people are detained without trial.

events.title: The Guerrilla Girls Appear
events.body: Anonymous women artists in gorilla masks start fly-posting SoHo with statistics about how few women and artists of colour the galleries show. Their guerrilla posters go on to shame museums for decades.

events.title: “Between the Wars”
events.body: Billy Bragg's plain-spoken ballad for the mining communities, released as the strike collapses — a folk song for the post-industrial north.

events.title: “Sun City”
events.body: Steven Van Zandt gathers more than fifty artists — Springsteen, Miles Davis, Run-DMC, Bono — as Artists United Against Apartheid to vow they will never play South Africa's Sun City resort.

events.title: Free South Africa
events.body: Keith Haring's poster — a giant black figure towering over a small white one — is printed in thousands and handed out at anti-apartheid rallies. Haring believed art belonged on streets and subway walls, not only in galleries.

events.title: The Handmaid's Tale
events.body: Margaret Atwood imagines an America turned theocracy, its fertile women reduced to breeders. She said she used nothing that had not already happened somewhere — including the reversal of women's freedoms in Iran after 1979.

events.title: Boris Becker Wins Wimbledon
events.body: Boris Becker, aged 17, becomes the youngest man and first unseeded player to win the Wimbledon singles title. The victory reshapes European tennis and inspires a generation of German players.

events.title: Rainbow Warrior Bombing
events.body: French intelligence agents sink the Greenpeace vessel Rainbow Warrior in Auckland Harbour, killing photographer Fernando Pereira. The attack causes a major diplomatic crisis between France and New Zealand.

events.title: Coca-Cola Classic Returns
events.body: Seventy-nine days after New Coke, the company surrenders to public fury and brings back the original formula — one of marketing's great humiliations, and recoveries.

events.title: Live Aid
events.body: A dual-venue concert at Wembley and JFK Stadium broadcasts live to an estimated 1.9 billion viewers. Queen's performance is widely regarded as the greatest live rock set ever recorded. The event raises approximately £150 million for Ethiopian famine relief.

events.title: Madonna's Virgin Tour Begins
events.body: Madonna launches her first headline concert tour in Seattle, cementing her transition from pop star to cultural phenomenon and establishing a template for pop spectacle.

events.title: Titanic Wreck Located
events.body: Dr Robert Ballard locates the wreck of the RMS Titanic on the floor of the North Atlantic, 73 years after it sank, using remotely operated underwater vehicles — then cutting-edge technology.

events.title: Mexico City Earthquake
events.body: An 8.1 magnitude earthquake strikes Mexico City, killing an estimated 10,000 people. The government's slow response catalyses a civil society movement that reshapes Mexican politics toward democratic reform.

events.title: Plaza Accord Signed
events.body: Finance ministers of France, West Germany, Japan, the US, and UK agree to depreciate the US dollar. The accord reshapes global trade and triggers Japan's asset price bubble — with consequences echoing through the 1990s.

events.title: Rock Hudson Dies of AIDS
events.body: Hollywood actor Rock Hudson becomes the first major public figure to die of AIDS-related complications, bringing the crisis into global consciousness and accelerating US government attention to the epidemic.

events.title: Achille Lauro Hijacking
events.body: Palestinian militants hijack the cruise liner Achille Lauro and murder American passenger Leon Klinghoffer. The incident prompts a dramatic US military interception of the Egyptian aircraft carrying the hijackers.

events.title: Les Misérables Opens in London
events.body: The RSC's musical of Hugo's novel opens at the Barbican to sniffy reviews — and becomes the longest-running musical in West End history.

events.title: Back to the Future in UK Cinemas
events.body: Robert Zemeckis's Back to the Future becomes the highest-grossing film of 1985. Its portrait of 1955 America seen through 1985 eyes captures the nostalgia and anxiety of the Reagan era.

events.title: Nevado del Ruiz Eruption
events.body: The Nevado del Ruiz volcano in Colombia triggers mudflows burying the town of Armero, killing approximately 23,000 people — the deadliest volcanic disaster of the 20th century after Pelee in 1902.

events.title: Reagan–Gorbachev Geneva Summit
events.body: Reagan and Gorbachev meet for the first US-Soviet summit in six years, agreeing that 'a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought' — beginning a thaw that culminates in the INF Treaty of 1987.

events.title: Windows 1.0 Ships
events.body: Microsoft ships Windows 1.0. Initial reception is muted, but the graphical interface model it introduces becomes the template for personal computing for decades. Bill Gates has just turned 30.

events.title: The Color Purple Released
events.body: Spielberg's adaptation of Alice Walker's novel receives 11 Oscar nominations and marks a turning point in Hollywood's engagement with Black American stories. Oprah Winfrey makes her film debut.

events.title: Rome and Vienna Airport Attacks
events.body: Simultaneous attacks on El Al and TWA desks at Rome and Vienna airports kill 19 people. Attributed to the Abu Nidal Organisation, the attacks intensify debate about aviation security and state-sponsored terrorism.

events.title: Space Shuttle Challenger Disaster
events.body: Challenger breaks apart 73 seconds after launch, killing all seven crew members including schoolteacher Christa McAuliffe. Watched live by millions of schoolchildren, it grounds the shuttle programme for nearly three years.

events.title: Jean-Claude Duvalier Flees Haiti
events.body: 'Baby Doc' Duvalier flees into exile in France following mass uprisings, ending nearly 30 years of Duvalier family dictatorship.

events.title: The Channel Tunnel Treaty
events.body: Thatcher and Mitterrand sign the Treaty of Canterbury, committing Britain and France to dig under the Channel — ending ten centuries of moat.

events.title: Mir Space Station Launched
events.body: The Soviet Union launches the core module of Mir — the first consistently inhabited long-term research station in space, hosting crews from multiple nations over its 15-year operational life.

events.title: People Power Revolution — Philippines
events.body: Four days of nonviolent uprisings on EDSA in Manila force President Ferdinand Marcos to flee. Corazon Aquino is sworn in as President. The revolution becomes a model for nonviolent regime change studied worldwide.

events.title: Top Gun Released
events.body: Tony Scott's Top Gun becomes the highest-grossing film of 1986. Its glossy militarism defines a strand of Reagan-era American self-image. US Navy recruiting stations report a significant spike in applications following its release.

events.title: Halley's Comet at Perihelion
events.body: Halley's Comet reaches its closest approach to the sun. The ESA's Giotto spacecraft flies within approximately 600 kilometres of the comet's nucleus, returning the first close-up images of a cometary core.

events.title: Cohabitation Begins in France
events.body: Socialist President Mitterrand appoints Gaullist Jacques Chirac as Prime Minister — the first 'cohabitation' in the French Fifth Republic. The experiment reshapes understanding of French constitutional arrangements.

events.title: La Belle Discotheque Bombing, Berlin
events.body: A bomb planted by Libyan intelligence explodes at La Belle discotheque in West Berlin, killing three people and wounding approximately 230. The attack directly triggers the US bombing of Libya nine days later.

events.title: US Bombs Libya
events.body: The US launches airstrikes against Tripoli and Benghazi in response to the La Belle bombing, killing an estimated 45 people. The operation marks a significant escalation in US willingness to conduct unilateral military action against state sponsors of terrorism.

events.title: Chernobyl Nuclear Disaster
events.body: Reactor Number Four at Chernobyl explodes, causing the worst nuclear accident in history. The Soviet government's delayed response accelerates public loss of faith in the state — contributing to the forces that ultimately dissolve the USSR.

events.title: Maradona: Hand of God & Goal of the Century
events.body: Diego Maradona scores two of the most famous goals in football history against England at the 1986 World Cup quarter-final — one with his hand, the other a 60-metre solo run past five defenders subsequently voted the Goal of the Century.

events.title: Argentina Win 1986 World Cup
events.body: Argentina defeat West Germany 3–2 in the final in Mexico City. Maradona wins the Golden Ball. The tournament is remembered as one of the greatest in the competition's history.

events.title: The Butcher Boys
events.body: Jane Alexander, still a student, makes three seated figures with human bodies, horns and sealed mouths. Made during the states of emergency, they are a portrait of the violence the country was trying not to see.

events.title: Maus
events.body: Art Spiegelman draws his father's survival of Auschwitz with Jews as mice and Nazis as cats. The first volume changes what comics can be; the complete work wins a Pulitzer Prize in 1992.

events.title: South Africa: Nationwide State of Emergency
events.body: The South African government extends its state of emergency to the entire country. More than 26,000 people are detained over the following two years, intensifying both internal resistance and international isolation of the apartheid regime.

events.title: Lake Nyos Disaster
events.body: Lake Nyos in Cameroon releases a massive cloud of carbon dioxide, asphyxiating approximately 1,800 people and 3,500 livestock — one of the few known mass asphyxiations caused by a natural event.

events.title: Pan Am Flight 73 Hijacking
events.body: Four Palestinian gunmen hijack Pan Am Flight 73 at Karachi airport. After a 16-hour standoff, 20 people are killed. Flight attendant Neerja Bhanot dies shielding children from gunfire and is posthumously awarded India's highest peacetime gallantry honour.

events.title: Tutu Enthroned in Cape Town
events.body: Desmond Tutu becomes the first black Archbishop of Cape Town, head of southern Africa's Anglicans — and apartheid's most eloquent opponent in a cassock.

events.title: Watchmen
events.body: Alan Moore and Dave Gibbons' twelve-issue comic imagines superheroes in a 1985 where Nixon is still president and the Doomsday Clock stands at five to midnight — a graphic novel steeped in the nuclear fear of the Reagan years.

events.title: Iran–Contra Affair Breaks
events.body: The Lebanese magazine Ash-Shiraa reveals the US has been secretly selling arms to Iran and using proceeds to fund Contra rebels in Nicaragua, circumventing a Congressional ban. The most serious political crisis of the Reagan presidency.

events.title: Reykjavik Summit
events.body: Reagan and Gorbachev come remarkably close to agreeing elimination of all nuclear weapons before talks collapse over Reagan's refusal to abandon his Strategic Defense Initiative. The summit accelerates momentum toward the INF Treaty signed the following year.

events.title: Phantom of the Opera Opens in London
events.body: Andrew Lloyd Webber's The Phantom of the Opera opens at Her Majesty's Theatre. It becomes the longest-running show in Broadway history when it transfers to New York in 1988.

events.title: The Big Bang
events.body: London's financial markets deregulate overnight — electronic trading, foreign banks, the end of the old City. Modern global finance starts here.

events.title: Mike Tyson Becomes Heavyweight Champion
events.body: Mike Tyson, aged 20, knocks out Trevor Berbick to become the youngest heavyweight champion in boxing history. His speed, power, and ferocity make him appear almost invincible for the next four years.

events.title: Chinese Student Democracy Protests
events.body: Students at universities across China begin protests demanding democratic reforms. They are suppressed without major violence but lead to the forced resignation of Communist Party General Secretary Hu Yaobang — whose death in 1989 will spark the Tiananmen Square protests.

events.title: Andrei Sakharov Released from Exile
events.body: Soviet physicist and human rights activist Andrei Sakharov is released from seven years of internal exile under Gorbachev's glasnost policy. His release is a powerful signal of genuine change in the Soviet Union.

events.title: Voyager Completes Round-the-World Flight
events.body: The experimental aircraft Voyager, piloted by Dick Rutan and Jeana Yeager, completes the first non-stop, non-refuelled circumnavigation of the Earth in approximately 9 days, landing with less than 18 litres of fuel remaining.

events.title: Andy Warhol Dies
events.body: The king of Pop Art dies unexpectedly at 58 after gallbladder surgery in New York. His estate funds a foundation that still shapes contemporary art.

events.title: Supernova 1987A
events.body: Light from an exploding star in the Large Magellanic Cloud reaches Earth — the nearest observed supernova in 383 years, and a bonanza for astronomy.

events.title: Zeebrugge Disaster
